decisions.evidence: R3 maker: 'paste this link ... Press Save ... the link is saved immediately'; R3 client accepts the save box. Save-by-url conforms to reference.
decisions.note: Prototype review. Core save-by-url presented and conforming to REF-BM-01.

decisions.evidence: R3 maker: 'I filled in three things automatically — the page title, a one-line description, and the site name. Is that the right set?' (no favicon, no preview image). R3 client: 'I want the page title, short description, actual site icon, a preview image when the page provides one, and the date I saved it.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Presented metadata set omits favicon and preview image required by REF-BM-02; client requests the missing reference metadata (extend).

decisions.evidence: R3 maker: instant save with no review/edit step ('the link is saved immediately'). R3 client: 'I should be able to adjust the title and description before confirming the save, as well as edit them later, because automatically gathered details are not always helpful.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. R3 lacked edit-before-save; client requests editing before and after saving per REF-BM-03. Delivered as inline review panel in R4.

decisions.evidence: R3 maker presents immediate save with no duplicate handling ('Feel free to save a second link too'). R3 client: 'If I save a link that is already in my library, don't create a duplicate. Take me to the existing entry so I can edit it instead.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. R3 omits dedup; client requests convergence-to-edit-existing per REF-BM-06. R4 delivers it and R4 client extends with duplicate-blocking on address edit (same requirement).

decisions.evidence: R3/R4 maker: 'saved links listed below it as cards' exposing title, description, tags, favicon. R3 client: 'the calm card layout feel right'.
decisions.note: Prototype review. Readability-first list conforms to REF-BM-07 (orthogonal card-vs-row layout not a divergence).

decisions.evidence: R4 maker: 'the saved card's title links to the real https://nytimes.com'; R4 client: 'accepting nytimes.com behave as I'd expect'.
decisions.note: Prototype review. Selecting item navigates to original url per REF-BM-08; conforming.

decisions.evidence: R4 maker: 'Editing (both before saving and later) covers the title and description only — not the web address itself. Is that the right boundary, or should the address be editable too?' R4 client: 'The address should also be editable later. If I change it, I'd expect the app to fetch the new page's details ... preserving any title or description I deliberately wrote'.
decisions.note: Prototype review. Presented edit scope excludes url; client requests url editability (with re-fetch) per REF-BM-04 (edit url/title/description/tags/note). Delivered R5, conforming.

decisions.evidence: R7-R8 maker: 'To read' vs Reference tabs with counts, 'Mark as read' removes from To-read view while item stays in library. R8 client: 'that matches my intent'.
decisions.note: Prototype review. Unread flag, separate unread view, and mark-read removal conform to REF-BM-17/18/19. The client's default-shelf and read-item-resting-place refinements (R7) are orthogonal to reference items (no 'Reference' shelf in spec) and excluded.

decisions.evidence: R9 maker: 'Type cables, press Enter (it becomes a chip) ... The card shows your #cables #internet tags.' R9 client: 'The tag-chip interaction feels natural'.
decisions.note: Prototype review. Assigning one or more tags conforms to REF-BM-09.

decisions.evidence: R9 maker: 'click its #database tag chip. The library narrows to everything tagged database'. R9 client endorses tag filtering (asks only that it stay in current view — orthogonal).
decisions.note: Prototype review. Select-tag-to-filter conforms to REF-BM-11; the jump-to-All vs stay-in-view point is a functionally-equivalent scoping preference, excluded.

decisions.evidence: R9 maker presents tag entry as type+Enter chip with no suggestions. R9 client: 'when I start typing I want suggestions from tags I've already used, so I can reuse them ... instead of accidentally creating near-duplicates.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. R9 tag entry lacks autocomplete of existing tags; client requests it per REF-BM-10 (extend).

decisions.evidence: R9 maker: 'Search looks across the title, description, site name, and tags' (no url, no note). R9 client: 'It should ... search the title, description, web address, and any personal note I add to a bookmark.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Presented search omits url and note fields required by REF-BM-12; client extends to include them.

decisions.evidence: R9 maker presents search with no statement of case handling. R9 client: 'It should ignore capitalization'.
decisions.note: Prototype review. Case-insensitive search (REF-BM-13) absent from presented behavior; client requests it (extend). Reinforced at R10 for operators.

decisions.evidence: R9 maker presents only tag-chip click filtering, no #tag search syntax. R9 client: 'Typing #database should specifically search that tag.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. #tag search syntax (REF-BM-14) missing; client extends. Delivered R10.

decisions.evidence: R9 maker: multi-word = AND only, 'The current simple search is a good starting point.' R9 client: 'I want to combine searches with AND, OR, NOT, and parentheses—for example, rome (#article OR #book) ... putting it in quotation marks should treat it as ordinary text.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Boolean/parentheses grammar and quoted-operator-literal rule (REF-BM-15) absent; client requests the full grammar (extend).

decisions.evidence: R9 maker presents no phrase matching. R9 client: 'Quotation marks should find an exact phrase.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Quoted-phrase exact match (REF-BM-16) missing; client extends. Delivered R10.

decisions.evidence: R10 maker: 'AND/OR/NOT act as operators only in capitals — lowercase or is treated as an ordinary word'. R10 client: 'I would not make the operators depend on capitalization. AND, and, And should behave the same ... Quoting the word ... should be the one clear way to search for it literally.'
decisions.note: Implementation/spec review. Revised presentation introduces a new divergence: uppercase-only operators contradict REF-BM-15 (example uses lowercase 'or'; only quoting makes an operator literal) and REF-BM-13. Client supplies the reference-conforming rule (correct). Distinct decision from R9 absence.

decisions.evidence: R10 maker adds a plain 'Your note' field ('did you mean the Description itself is your note?'), no formatting. R10 client: 'The note should be editable, support Markdown-style formatting, and display that formatting when I view the bookmark.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Presented note lacks markdown rendering required by REF-BM-23; client extends with markdown support. Delivered R11.

decisions.evidence: R12 maker: archive hides from All/To-read/Reference and searches, Archived tab with Restore, permanent Delete only in archive behind confirmation. R12 client: 'This structure feels right ... I'm happy to lock in this archive-and-delete behavior.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Archive hiding (REF-BM-26), archive-vs-delete distinction (REF-BM-27), separate archived list (REF-BM-28), and delete (REF-BM-05) all conform. Client's 'search archived-only within archive' refinement is consistent with the reference edge rule.

decisions.evidence: R13 maker: 'that completes the exploration, and I'll summarize the whole settled scope'. R13 client: 'I don't think exploration is complete yet ... Selecting several links and acting on them together: add or remove tags, mark read or unread, archive, or delete. I should also be able to apply an action to every link matching the current search, tag, or view.'
decisions.note: Specification gate. Maker moved to conclude scope omitting bulk actions; client extends with REF-BM-20 (multi-select bulk actions) and REF-BM-21 (apply-to-whole-matching-set). Delivered R16.

decisions.evidence: R13 client (contesting 'exploration complete'): 'Choosing how links are sorted, such as by date added or title.' (Earlier foreshadowed R3: 'I'd eventually like to choose a different order'.)
decisions.note: Specification gate. Sort-by-key (REF-BM-22) not in about-to-settle scope; client extends. Delivered R14 (Newest/Oldest/Title A-Z/Z-A); the 'Recently updated' addition is beyond-spec and not a reference divergence.

decisions.evidence: R13 client: 'Saving a reusable view made from search words plus tags to include or exclude.'
decisions.note: Specification gate. Saved bundle (REF-BM-29) omitted from about-to-settle scope; client extends. Delivered R18 conforming (dynamic, search + include/exclude tags, no pinned reading state).

decisions.evidence: R13 client: 'Importing and exporting standard browser-bookmark HTML while retaining titles, tags, and original saved dates.'
decisions.note: Specification gate. Netscape import (REF-BM-30) omitted; client extends. Delivered R19; the R19/R20 folder-to-tag mapping is beyond-spec and excluded.

decisions.evidence: R13 client: 'Importing and exporting standard browser-bookmark HTML while retaining titles, tags, and original saved dates.'
decisions.note: Specification gate. Netscape export (REF-BM-31) omitted from about-to-settle scope; client extends. Delivered R19 conforming.

decisions.evidence: R13 client: 'Personal display choices such as the default order, how many links are shown, and text size.'
decisions.note: Specification gate. Display preferences (REF-BM-32) omitted; client extends. Delivered R22 (default order, links per page, text size) conforming; cross-device sync is beyond/infra and excluded.

decisions.evidence: R16 maker: '"Select all N shown" ... it grabs exactly the currently-showing set.' R16 client: '"Select all" must mean every link matching the current view, search, and tag filters—even when only one page of results is visible. I'd label it "Select all N matching".'
decisions.note: Implementation review. Revised presentation diverges: select-all scoped to visible page contradicts REF-BM-21 (whole matching collection). Client supplies the reference-conforming scope (correct). Distinct implementation-stage divergence from the R13 scope request; reaffirmed R22 for pagination.

decisions.evidence: R16 maker: bulk 'Add tag is a typed box' with no suggestions. R16 client: 'The add-tag box should offer my existing tags as I type, just like the tag field when saving.'
decisions.note: Implementation review. The bulk add-tag control lacks the existing-tag autocomplete of REF-BM-10; client extends. Same reference item as R9, different location/stage.

decisions.evidence: Requested R13: 'Keeping a preserved copy of a page, with PDFs stored as PDFs'. R21 maker: snapshot 'Simulated here ... I'd propose this area become its own cycle'. R21 client: '"Save a copy" should create a self-contained local HTML file for a normal page, while a PDF address should store the original PDF ... I'm comfortable recording the actual page storage ... as a separate follow-up cycle.'
decisions.note: Implementation review. Reference REF-BM-24 (local single-file snapshot; PDF-as-PDF rule) is only simulated and its real implementation is deferred to a later cycle. Client explicitly states the exact expected reference behavior and accepts the departure (deferral) without requesting alignment in this cycle → accepted_divergence.

decisions.evidence: Requested R13: 'optionally sending a copy to the Internet Archive'. R21 maker: 'Send to Internet Archive ... Simulated here ... its own cycle'. R21 client: 'The Internet Archive link should appear only after the service confirms that a snapshot exists ... I'm comfortable recording the actual ... Internet Archive connection as a separate follow-up cycle.'
decisions.note: Implementation review. Reference REF-BM-25 (Internet Archive snapshot) is simulated and deferred. Client explicitly expresses the expected behavior (link only after confirmation) and accepts deferral without requesting cycle-1 alignment → accepted_divergence.
